record.question: Which of the following is a commonly used preservative in ophthalmic preparations?
record.explanation: Answer D: Benzalkonium chloride. Benzalkonium chloride is a commonly used antimicrobial preservative in multidose ophthalmic products; sodium chloride is primarily a tonicity agent. Source/context note: Not every ophthalmic preparation uses a preservative; single-dose products often are preservative-free. Reference: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?query=benzalkonium%20chloride%20ophthalmic. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
